title: What Chicago style is
summary: He says Chicago style is Dixieland played in four beats to the bar, with spirit.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Let's talk a little bit about some of these marvellous albums that you have made. I think before we do that, when I first started talking to you today I said that you were a representative of the Chicago jazz style.

And I'm wondering if you might want to do a little explicating here for us or illuminating here for us so that other people who are not familiar with these various delineations would know how one distinguishes jazz, I mean the Chicago style from the New Orleans style....
The category in which people put names on and so forth. It's pretty tough to do because actually Chicago style is really swing. Benny Goodman put the name on it, the moniker on it or

the label so to speak when he said swing. Because when you play a dixieland number it has to be a dixieland number. Written by a dixielander you know, style. But we played dixieland in a swing style. Now that's about the only way I can say it or it's like a melodic number, 'it's wonderful you know. 'It's Wonderful, it's Marvellous'. But we'd play it swing style. Which is four beats to the bar for the drums and for the bass instead of two beats, two beats to the bar you know. Bump, Bump, Bump, Bump. We play, bump, bump, bump, bump. (IMITATES TWO AND FOUR BEATS TO THE BAR)................ Four beats to the bar. Which makes it swing. That's swing.

Where old Dixieland used to be in the two beat. Now that's the only thing that we did that brought us shall we say out of the dixieland style. They have a name for it. So, but the one thing that we had, the Chicago crowd including Benny Goodman, Muggsy Spanier and everybody is that we had a lot of spirit. And we loved to play more than anything. That was it.. We just loved to play and we'd play all the time.
